page: Amazon Web Services c7g.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the 64-bit ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 architecture. The instance provides 16 dedicated physical cores running at 2.6 GHz with one thread per core, backed by 64 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per processor structure. It is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard compute-optimized 1:2 core-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs included, and no local NVMe storage is bundled, relying exclusively on network-attached storage over an 8 Gbps baseline network link.

Benchmark results demonstrate solid general throughput alongside standout memory subsystem performance. The instance achieved a top-tier PassMark memory score of 2972.27 and strong large-block uncached memory write bandwidth of 93.97 GB/sec. General compute benchmarks show balanced middle-tier outcomes, including a PassMark CPU score of 11483.62, a Geekbench multi-core score of 12798.0, and 24503.13 on stress-ng multi-core testing. In-memory operations yielded 26.15 million Redis SET operations per second, while static web serving throughput reached 28.48 GB/sec.

Performance constraints appear in cryptographic tasks and heavier compute workloads. The PassMark CPU encryption benchmark scored in the bottom 25% at 2226.35, and prompt processing for medium-scale 7B parameter models reached 28.19 tokens/sec, placing in the lower quartile. The architecture omits x86-specific vector instruction sets like AVX-512 and AMX, focusing hardware capability through native ARM instructions and hardware AES.

The Graviton-based design delivers efficient per-core resource density without simultaneous multithreading penalties. It is suitable for batch processing, web serving clusters, Clang build compilation farms, and distributed caching nodes that benefit from strong memory bandwidth without demanding local storage or dedicated graphics hardware.
description: Amazon Web Services c7g.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance based on the 64-bit ARM Neoverse-V1 architecture and the Nitro hypervisor. The instance features 16 dedicated physical cores at 2.6 GHz without multithreading, alongside 32.0 GB of system memory (2.0 GB per vCPU) and an 8 Gbps network baseline. It contains no local storage and no GPU accelerators. In benchmarks, the c7g.4xlarge demonstrates top-tier memory scores in PassMark (2972.27) and strong uncached write bandwidth of 93.97 GB/sec, while maintaining average multi-core compute throughput across stress-ng and Geekbench. Cryptographic and heavier prompt-processing workloads show lower relative efficiency. The system provides cost-effective dedicated compute capacity for code compilation, distributed caching, web serving, and containerized microservices.
